groups.instructions: Read the notice and complete the numbered blanks.
groups.passage:
Evening Bird Survey

The nature club is organising a bird survey in the park. Anyone aged fifteen or older can participate, even if they have no previous -------(21)------- of identifying birds. At the start, a volunteer will demonstrate how to use the recording sheet. Participants should remain quiet so that the birds are less likely -------(22)------- away. Each group will be assigned a small area, and all sightings must be written down -------(23)------- the same format. Please bring a pencil and a bottle of water. In the event of heavy rain, the survey will be -------(24)------- until the following evening. The results will be shared with the park team, -------(25)------- uses them to plan future habitat improvements.

A Smaller School Lunch Queue

A school introduced staggered lunch periods after students complained that they were spending too much of their break waiting for food. The new timetable divides pupils into three groups, each of -------(26)------- has a different starting time. Staff initially worried that the change might -------(27)------- with afternoon lessons. However, teachers helped adjust the schedule so that every class still received the same amount of teaching time. Students now spend less time queuing and have longer to eat, -------(28)------- the kitchen does not need to serve everyone at once. The school is collecting feedback -------(29)------- deciding whether the arrangement should become permanent. One question is whether younger pupils feel as -------(30)------- with the change as older pupils do.

groups.instructions: Read the article and answer the questions.
groups.passage:
An Extra Stop for the Community Bus

A village bus used to stop only beside the main road. Although the stop was convenient for residents near the market, people living beyond the hill had a long walk. A group of residents suggested adding a stop near a housing estate. The transport company agreed to test the idea for three months.

The trial added four minutes to each journey. To avoid missed connections with trains, the company adjusted the departure time from the village slightly. Drivers also collected information about the number of passengers joining at the new stop and the time needed for boarding.

At the end of the trial, the company found that more residents were using the bus, particularly on weekdays. However, the timetable change had caused difficulty for a few workers starting early shifts. The company arranged a separate discussion with these workers before deciding how to revise the permanent schedule.

questions.question_text: What problem did some villagers have before the trial?

options.text: They could not buy train tickets.
They had no access to the market.
They were required to change buses twice.
They had a long walk to the bus stop.

questions.explanation: Đoạn đầu nói người sống bên kia đồi phải đi bộ xa đến điểm dừng.
questions.translation: Một số dân làng gặp vấn đề gì trước khi thử nghiệm?

questions.question_text: How long was the new stop tested?

questions.translation: Điểm dừng mới được thử trong bao lâu?

groups.instructions: Read the article and answer the questions.
groups.passage:
Learning from Food Waste

A secondary school wanted to reduce the amount of food thrown away in its dining hall. Rather than beginning with posters telling pupils to eat everything, the catering team first measured which dishes were most frequently left unfinished. They also asked students why they did not finish particular meals.

The responses revealed several different causes. Some pupils disliked certain flavours, while others reported that servings were too large. A few had simply run out of time before the end of lunch. These findings suggested that a single instruction to waste less would have limited effect.

The team introduced a smaller serving as an optional choice. Students selecting it could return for an additional portion if they were still hungry. Kitchen staff also adjusted the preparation of one unpopular vegetable dish after a tasting session. During the following month, the weight of leftovers fell, while the number of meals served remained similar.

The school recognised that reducing leftovers was only one measure of success. It also needed to ensure that pupils were eating enough. A reduction achieved because students skipped lunch would be a poor outcome. The team therefore continued to monitor participation and collect feedback about hunger and satisfaction.

questions.question_text: Why did the catering team measure unfinished dishes first?

options.text: To decide how to charge for leftovers.
To identify which foods were commonly wasted.
To calculate the number of school teachers.
To discourage all pupils from eating lunch.

questions.translation: Vì sao nhóm phục vụ đo lượng thức ăn thừa trước?

questions.question_text: Which reason for leaving food was mentioned in paragraph 2?

options.text: Students were prohibited from drinking water.

questions.explanation: Đoạn hai nêu một số học sinh nhận khẩu phần quá lớn.
questions.translation: Lý do nào được nêu trong đoạn hai?

questions.question_text: What could students do after choosing a smaller serving?

options.text: Ask for more if they were still hungry.

questions.explanation: Đoạn ba nêu có thể quay lại nhận thêm nếu vẫn đói.
questions.translation: Học sinh có thể làm gì sau khi chọn phần nhỏ?

options.text: It would increase the number of meals served.

options.text: Waste reduction should consider both causes and pupils' nutrition.
Every pupil should be forced to finish a large meal.

questions.translation: Nhận định nào phản ánh thông điệp chính của tác giả?

groups.instructions: Read the essay and answer the questions.
groups.passage:
When Students Become Weather Observers

A weather station installed in a school garden can provide more than figures for a science lesson. Students may use it to examine how measurements are made, how local conditions vary and how evidence supports a conclusion. But the educational value of a station depends on the questions pupils ask and the care with which they collect information.

At one school, two classes began comparing daily temperatures. Their thermometers were of the same model, yet the figures differed. One instrument stood beside a wall that received afternoon sunshine, while the other was located in an open grassy area. Pupils initially thought that one thermometer was faulty. After exchanging the instruments, they noticed that the higher readings continued to occur near the wall. The difference was therefore more likely to reflect the measurement locations.

This observation led to a wider discussion about sampling. If students wanted to estimate the temperature of the garden as a whole, one convenient location might be insufficient. If their aim was to understand where pupils could find cooler places during lunch, the contrast between locations was valuable in its own right. The suitability of a measurement depended on the question being investigated.

The classes also learned to record uncertainty. When strong winds damaged a sensor, one group left a gap in its records and explained the reason. Another group suggested filling the gap with an average from neighbouring days. The teacher explained that an estimated value could be useful in a later calculation, provided that it was clearly identified as an estimate. An apparently complete table could otherwise hide a significant weakness.

At the end of the term, the students presented their findings. Their displays included photographs of instrument locations, explanations of missing values and examples of conclusions that the data could support. The teacher praised the groups for explaining their methods openly. Their work demonstrated that collecting measurements is only part of an investigation: deciding what those measurements represent is equally important.

questions.question_text: According to paragraph 1, what determines the educational value of a weather station?

options.text: The accuracy of the equipment regardless of the investigation.
The number of locations measured regardless of the purpose.
The completeness of the temperature table alone.
The questions students investigate and their care in collecting information.

questions.explanation: Đoạn đầu xác định câu hỏi và sự cẩn thận khi thu thập thông tin là yếu tố quyết định.
questions.translation: Theo đoạn một, điều gì quyết định giá trị giáo dục của trạm thời tiết?

questions.question_text: Why did the pupils exchange the thermometers?

options.text: To compare readings taken at different times of day.
To check whether the wall changed temperature after the instruments moved.
To test whether the instruments caused the difference in readings.
To establish which thermometer consistently produced higher readings without changing its location.

questions.explanation: Đoạn hai cho biết học sinh nghi một nhiệt kế hỏng nên đổi vị trí để kiểm tra.
questions.translation: Vì sao học sinh đổi hai nhiệt kế cho nhau?

questions.question_text: What happened after the thermometers were exchanged?

options.text: Higher readings followed the thermometer originally near the wall.
The grassy area became consistently warmer.
Higher readings still occurred near the wall.

questions.explanation: Đoạn hai nêu số đo cao hơn vẫn xuất hiện gần tường.
questions.translation: Điều gì xảy ra sau khi đổi nhiệt kế?

questions.question_text: The word “insufficient” in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to -------.
questions.explanation: Insufficient nghĩa là không đủ cho mục đích đặt ra.
questions.translation: Từ insufficient gần nghĩa nhất với cụm nào?

questions.question_text: When would contrasting readings from different locations be especially useful?

options.text: When calculating a whole-garden average from one location alone.
When investigating where pupils can find cooler places.
When testing whether the two thermometers have identical readings in the same location.
When estimating temperatures on days with missing sensor records.

questions.explanation: Đoạn ba nêu ví dụ xác định nơi mát hơn vào giờ trưa.
questions.translation: Khi nào các số đo khác nhau giữa vị trí đặc biệt hữu ích?

questions.question_text: What condition did the teacher place on the use of estimated values?

options.text: They must be clearly identified as estimates.
They must be calculated only from the same instrument before it broke.
They must be recorded as measured values if the average is plausible.
They must be excluded from every later calculation.

questions.explanation: Đoạn bốn cho phép số ước tính nếu được ghi rõ là ước tính.
questions.translation: Giáo viên đặt điều kiện gì cho việc dùng giá trị ước tính?

questions.question_text: What can be inferred about the teacher's priorities?

options.text: The completeness of the data table is the main measure of quality.
Transparent methods are more important than an apparently perfect table.
Agreement between instruments matters more than the measurement purpose.
A location photograph is sufficient to justify any conclusion.

questions.explanation: Giáo viên khen việc trình bày phương pháp công khai và cảnh báo bảng đầy đủ có thể che giấu điểm yếu.
questions.translation: Có thể suy ra điều gì về ưu tiên của giáo viên?

questions.question_text: Which title best captures the central idea?

options.text: Selecting a Representative Location for Every Weather Station
Replacing Missing Temperature Readings with Averages
Comparing the Accuracy of Two School Thermometers
What School Weather Measurements Can Teach Us About Evidence

questions.explanation: Bài bàn về việc hiểu phương pháp, vị trí, độ bất định và ý nghĩa của bằng chứng.
questions.translation: Tiêu đề nào thể hiện đúng ý chính?
